feed.title: QSAVE post-quantum solution for non-migrated coins

entry.title: QSAVE post-quantum solution for non-migrated coins
entry.summary:
The QSAVE initiative presents a series of proposals aimed at addressing the challenges posed by the transition to post-quantum cryptocurrency systems without necessitating the burning of coins. The strategy involves a detailed framework set forth in five draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposals (BIPs), which are accessible for review at the [QSAVE BIP Suite](https://www.qsave.org/legal/bip-suite). This suite includes various mechanisms such as conditional spending, watermarking pre-cutoff commitments, seed derivation factors, protective recovery processes, and the utilization of zero-knowledge scalable transparent argument of knowledge (zk-STARK) technology for transaction verification.
The proposed system classifies inputs into transactions based on whether they meet the criteria of having migrated to a quantum-resistant state. Inputs that have not been upgraded with a second factor are directed towards a protective recovery route, ensuring that these coins are not permanently lost but are instead held in a recoverable state. This is achieved through a decentralized network of custodians who manage these recovery outputs under strict conditions to prevent misuse or loss, while also potentially generating modest returns that could be directed towards charitable causes.
In the mechanism designed by QSAVE, two-factor authentication plays a critical role after a certain block height. From this point, the use of both the existing cryptographic key (whether quantum-derived or not) and a second proof—such as evidence that the address derives from the wallet seed or a binding record committed before a cutoff—are required to spend coins. Absence of this second factor means that the coins can only be transferred to a designated lost-property address, where they can remain indefinitely until legitimate recovery is possible either through on-chain or off-chain means.
This approach aims to offer a secure method to handle assets left behind during the migration to a post-quantum blockchain without forcing a burn of coins, thereby aligning with practices similar to those outlined in the Dormant Assets Act 2022 in the UK. By making use of both existing and new security measures, QSAVE's proposal intends to provide a balanced solution that respects the need for enhanced security in the face of quantum computing while ensuring that asset owners retain the ability to reclaim their property under new technological norms. This initiative reflects a proactive step towards adapting Bitcoin’s infrastructure to future technological challenges, potentially avoiding scenarios where unpreparedness leads to significant disruption or intervention by external parties.
